chunks: It is He who gives you life and death. When He creates a thing, He has only to say: "Be," and it is.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Allah's command 'Be' in creation?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ghafir is often cited to affirm Allah's absolute sovereignty (Tawhid al-Fi'l), illustrating that His will is the sole cause of existence without need for intermediate instruments. The phrase 'Kun fayakun' (Be, and it is) underscores the immediacy of divine command, a concept frequently linked to the Imams' role as the practical manifestation of God's will on earth. This highlights the seamless transition from divine decree to physical reality, reinforcing the belief in God's effortless power over life and death.
